absent: Guest page walker callback behavior and exception reporting for failed translations.
Special root allocation, shadow root allocation, obsolete root reclaim, and root synchronization details.
Vendor load paging base and flush current TLB effects and required ordering.
Two dimensional paging root allocation and mirrored translation lifecycle.
Obsolete page detection, oldest page zapping, and commit zap sequencing.
Reverse map head layout, iterator mechanics, and huge page level limits.
Shadow present, writable, MMU writable, and frame extraction predicates plus atomic update thresholds.
Per MMU entry sync callback behavior and guest reserved bit validation.
Write flooding detection policy and unsync child handling beyond counter reset.
Dirty logging, access tracking, and notifier interaction for unmap and protection changes.

findings.text: Shadow MMU sizing policy uses a memslot to MMU page ratio of fifty, a minimum allocation batch of sixty four, a hash width of twelve with table size derived as one shifted by that width, a low water mark of five free pages, and a refill target of twenty five.

Guest page table bit positions observed are present at bit zero, writable at bit one, user at bit two, write through at bit three, cache disable at bit four, accessed at bit five, dirty at bit six, page size and PAT at bit seven, global at bit eight, execute disable at bit sixty three, and directory PAT at bit twelve.
Paging root level identifiers are five for five level 64 bit paging, four for four level 64 bit paging, two for 32 bit paging, and three for 32 bit paging with extended entries.

Access tracking values map read to the present bit, write to the writable bit, and non extended user to the user bit, with a separate user execute alias used only for extended tables, an execute value of eight, and a combined all value covering execute plus write plus user plus read.

MMU role membership selects from control registers the paging extension, physical address extension, five level enable, supervisor execution prevention, supervisor access prevention and protection keys from CR4, plus paging and write protect from CR0, plus long mode enable and no execute enable from EFER.
A predicate reports mode based execute control support by inspecting the supervisor execution prevention flag held in the current MMU root role.

A guest virtual to guest physical helper performs a write oriented walk, requesting user permission when current privilege level equals three and always requesting write permission, delegating the walk to the per vcpu walker callback.

A thin wrapper requests unprotect and retry without forcing retry, while the full helper optionally records the failing instruction pointer and faulting address when work was done or when forced retry was requested.
Root reload first reclaims obsolete roots when requested, then returns success when the current root host address remains valid, otherwise it invokes full MMU load.
Page directory load publishes the current root host address and paging level to the vendor callback, and does nothing when the root host address is not a valid page.

Fragments observe a per vcpu MMU context with a root holding a host address and guest directory value, a root role descriptor with level and direct and protection flags, a mirrored root host address, a four entry PAE root table, and per VM counters for indirect pages, shadow pages, hash collisions and generation numbers.

Shadow page objects observed carry a guest frame number, a full role value, a pointer to the table storage, a root reference count, unsync and direct state, a write flooding counter, hash linkage, active list linkage, validity generation, and optional links for non present huge page handling and shadowed translations.

Full MMU load progresses through cache refill, special root allocation, direct or shadow root allocation depending on the direct flag, root synchronization, publication of the paging base, and a current TLB flush, aborting early on the first allocation failure.

Unprotect and retry moves from an unlocked fast check of the indirect page counter, to optional guest virtual to physical translation for indirect MMUs, to locked collection and commit of affected shadow pages, to recording retry state only when pages were zapped or retry was forced.

The unprotect path may read the indirect shadow page counter without holding the MMU lock purely as an optimization, then takes the MMU lock for writing while enumerating and zapping pages for the target frame.

Legacy direct root allocation holds the VM MMU lock for writing across page availability checks and root creation, while the two level direct path additionally depends on serialization that guarantees hash table presence before first root creation.

Reload treats the primary root host address as sufficient validity signal across three allowed combinations of mirrored and primary roots, and the fragments state that a valid primary with an invalid mirror never occurs.

Cache refill sizes request one plus maximum paging depth plus prefetch count for reverse map descriptors, maximum depth for external tables when mirrored translation is present, maximum depth for page headers and table storage, and maximum depth for shadowed info only when indirect mappings may be needed.

Memory cache refill returns immediately when the current object count already meets the minimum, allocates the pointer array once with the first requested capacity, rejects later capacity changes and conflicting zero or init settings, fills toward capacity, and only reports out of memory when the final count remains below the minimum.

Single object allocation prefers the configured slab cache when present, otherwise allocates one page, applies configured zeroing through allocation flags, and applies a configured fill pattern across the whole page when no slab cache is used.

Available page accounting subtracts used shadow pages from the configured maximum with saturation at zero, bypasses reclaim when at least five pages remain, otherwise zaps oldest pages toward the refill target and only fails when no page at all remains available.

Direct root creation uses the two level direct path when translation hardware is enabled, including optional mirrored root allocation, otherwise under lock it creates one root for four and five level modes or four quadrant roots for PAE mode while marking them present, and it clears the cached guest directory value because direct MMUs ignore it.

Root allocation derives its role from the current root role with overridden level and quadrant, warns on quadrant use without four byte entries and on direct use with four byte entries, reuses or creates the matching shadow page, and then increments that page root count while returning the physical address of its table.
Shadow page acquisition hashes only the guest frame number with a twelve bit hash, looks up the resulting bucket, allocates on miss, and emits a lookup trace distinguishing creation from reuse.

Bucket search skips obsolete pages, counts guest frame mismatches as collisions, zaps unsync pages when installing a higher level mapping for the same frame, returns direct matches immediately, attempts synchronization for unsync indirect matches with remote flush on success and rebuild on failure, and clears the flooding counter on reuse.

Synchronization compatibility rejects direct pages and missing per MMU sync callbacks, compares page role against current root role while ignoring level, access, quadrant and passthrough fields, and treats a role mismatch as a fatal programming warning.

Page synchronization first validates role compatibility, then visits every table entry while skipping never present entries, delegates present entries to the MMU specific sync callback, aggregates flush requests, and zaps the whole page when validation or an entry sync reports failure.

New shadow pages obtain header, table and optional shadowed info objects from caller caches, associate the table page with its header, join the hash bucket and the head of the active FIFO list, record guest frame and role and validity generation, and update accounting including indirect tracking when the page can hold guest entries.

Indirect accounting increments the indirect page counter before rereading guest entries with a full barrier, tracks writes for non leaf levels, and for leaf levels forbids large mappings and write protects the frame with a targeted remote flush when protection changed.

Frame write protection walks reverse map heads for eligible huge page levels plus the extended table walker when enabled, clears both host writable and MMU writable permissions as requested, and reports whether any caller must flush.

Shadow entry updates require the new value to be present, use a direct store when the old value was not present, otherwise select a fast or atomic slow update path, preserve the mapped frame across the update, and decide flush need from leaf level permission changes.

Several programming warnings signal corruption or misuse: capacity change or zero plus init conflict during cache setup, bad direct root level or missing PAE root storage, quadrant or direct role misuse, attempt to sync a direct page or mismatched context, reverse map walk reaching a non present entry, and entry update changing the mapped frame or clearing presence.

Reaching shadow page lookup without an initialized hash table is treated as fatal, and page availability handling deliberately allows brief overshoot of the configured maximum rather than failing guests when allocation needs up to four pages at once.
